caption: Fig.5.11 Aqueous solutions of complexes of nickel(II) with an increasing number of ethane-1, 2-diamine ligands.
note: text_layer null; read from the image. The caption is printed INSIDE target_box_in_crop, set as a block in the empty left half of the figure (not as a line under it), over six physical lines ('Fig.5.11' / 'Aqueous solutions of' / 'complexes of' / 'nickel(II) with an' / 'increasing number' / 'of ethane-1,' / '2-diamine ligands.') and is joined here with single spaces; note the book prints 'Fig.5.11' with NO colon and breaks 'ethane-1, 2-diamine' across a line after the comma, both copied as printed. Labels are read top-left to bottom-right: the two upper leader-line labels first (left, then right), then the two lower ones. Each label names one of the four test tubes in the drawn rack (green, pale blue, blue/purple, pink from left to right), connected to it by a black leader line; a flat list cannot carry which label points to which tube -- for the record, '[Ni(H2O)6]2+ (aq)' points to the green tube, '[Ni(H2O)4en]2+ (aq)' to the pale blue, '[Ni(H2O)4en2]2+ (aq)' to the blue/purple and '[Ni(en)3]2+ (aq)' to the pink. PRINTED AS SHOWN: the third label reads '[Ni(H2O)4en2]2+' with FOUR aqua ligands, although the reaction series printed just above this figure on the same page gives that species as [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+; re-checked at high zoom, the subscript is a 4, and it is copied as printed, not corrected. Notation: charges are printed as superscripts and counts as subscripts; both are flattened to plain characters ('[Ni(H2O)6]2+'), and 'en' is printed in lower case without parentheses in the figure labels (unlike the equations, which write '(en)'). Over-included by the crop and excluded as belonging to other blocks: the line above the box ('This sequence is shown in Fig. 5.11.') and, below it, the start of the 'Colour of Some Gem Stones' panel ('The colours produced by electronic transitions within the d orbitals of a transition metal ion occur frequently in everyday life. Ruby [Fig.5.12(a)] is ...'). A faint diagonal 'NCERT / not to be republished' watermark crosses the figure without obscuring any label; the figure and its caption are complete and unclipped.
